q: The tragedy 'Macbeth', centred on a Scottish general whose ambition, spurred by the prophecy of three witches, leads him to murder and tyranny, was written by:
e: Macbeth is a tragedy by William Shakespeare, in which the Scottish general Macbeth murders King Duncan after the witches' prophecy and is destroyed by his ambition.

q: The Damodaran Committee (2010), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India under the chairmanship of former SEBI Chairman M. Damodaran, was set up to look into:

options.A: The restructuring of Regional Rural Banks
options.D: The working of the money market

e: The RBI set up the Damodaran Committee in 2010, under former SEBI chairman M. Damodaran, specifically to examine customer service in banks and suggest improvements.

q: The first National Forest Commission of India, constituted in 2003 to review the forest and wildlife policy and legislation, was chaired by:
e: The first National Forest Commission, constituted in 2003 to review forest and wildlife policy and legislation, was chaired by former Chief Justice B. N. Kirpal.

q: The Hathi Committee (1975), appointed by the Government of India, was set up to examine and report on the working of the:
e: The Hathi Committee of 1975 examined the working of the drugs and pharmaceutical industry, including drug pricing, quality control and the role of foreign firms.

q: The Verghese Committee (1977), officially the Working Group on Autonomy for Akashvani and Doordarshan headed by B. G. Verghese, is best known for recommending:

options.A: The privatisation of radio and television broadcasting
options.B: Autonomy for All India Radio and Doordarshan through a national broadcast trust
options.C: The merger of All India Radio with Doordarshan
options.D: The abolition of external broadcast services

e: The Verghese Working Group on autonomy for Akashvani and Doordarshan recommended freeing them from direct government control through an autonomous national broadcast trust.

q: The Bhandari Committee (1994), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, was set up to recommend measures for the restructuring of:
e: The Bhandari Committee of 1994 was appointed by the RBI to recommend measures for restructuring the weak Regional Rural Banks and improving their viability.

q: The Baswan Committee (2015), constituted by the Government of India under the chairmanship of B. S. Baswan, was set up to review:

options.A: The pattern and syllabus of the Civil Services Examination conducted by the UPSC
options.B: The selection system of the Staff Selection Commission
options.C: The recruitment rules of the Railway Recruitment Boards
options.D: The examination system of the national universities

e: The Baswan Committee of 2015 reviewed the pattern, syllabus and related aspects of the UPSC Civil Services Examination, including age limits and attempts.

q: The Satish Chandra Committee (1989), appointed by the Union Public Service Commission, was set up to review:

options.A: The pay structure of Central Government employees
options.B: The cadre allocation policy of the All India Services
options.C: The system of selection to the civil services
options.D: The training curriculum at the national academies

e: The Satish Chandra Committee of 1989 was set up by the UPSC to review the system of selection to the civil services, following the earlier Kothari Committee reforms.

q: The Nigavekar Committee (2013), appointed by the Union Public Service Commission under the chairmanship of Prof. Arun Nigavekar, is associated with recommendations on:

options.A: The introduction of the Civil Services Aptitude Test
options.B: Changes in the pattern of the Civil Services (Main) Examination
options.C: The abolition of the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination
options.D: The raising of the upper age limit for the Civil Services Examination

e: The Nigavekar Committee, set up by the UPSC in 2013, is associated with recommendations on changes in the pattern of the Civil Services (Main) Examination.

q: The Jilani Committee (1992), a working group appointed by the Reserve Bank of India under the chairmanship of Rashid Jilani, is associated with recommendations on:

options.A: Internal control systems and internal inspection in banks
options.C: The licensing of new private sector banks

e: The Jilani Working Group of the RBI dealt with internal control systems and internal inspection in banks, including the role of internal audit and concurrent audit.

q: The Deepak Mohanty Committee (2015), appointed by the Reserve Bank of India, submitted its report on the medium-term path for:

options.A: The resolution of stressed assets of banks
options.B: The consolidation of public sector banks

e: The Deepak Mohanty Committee of 2015 submitted to the RBI its report on the medium-term path for financial inclusion, covering accounts, credit and digital access.

q: The Expenditure Reforms Commission, constituted by the Government of India in 2000, was chaired by:
e: The Expenditure Reforms Commission constituted in 2000 was chaired by K. P. Geethakrishnan, former Finance Secretary, to suggest cuts in government expenditure.

q: The Eradi Committee (1999), appointed by the Government of India under the chairmanship of Justice V. Balakrishna Eradi, was set up to examine the law relating to:

options.A: The settlement of inter-State water disputes
options.B: Insolvency and the winding up of companies
options.D: The regulation of the securities market

e: The Eradi Committee of 1999, chaired by Justice V. Balakrishna Eradi, examined the law relating to insolvency and winding up of companies and proposed a tribunal.

q: The headquarters of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) is located at:
e: The headquarters of NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, is in Brussels, Belgium, where its political headquarters and main institutions are located.

q: The Secretariat of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), one of its two standing bodies, is located at:
e: Beijing, China, hosts the Secretariat of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, one of the SCO's two standing bodies, the other being RATS in Tashkent.

q: The headquarters of the Commonwealth Secretariat, the principal intergovernmental agency of the Commonwealth of Nations, is located at:
e: The Commonwealth Secretariat, the main intergovernmental agency of the Commonwealth of Nations, is headquartered at Marlborough House in London.

q: World Food Day, marking the founding of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in 1945, is observed every year on:
e: World Food Day is observed on 16 October, the date on which the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations was founded in 1945.

q: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) in India, marking the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly, is observed every year on:
e: Constitution Day is observed on 26 November, the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India.

q: National Voters' Day in India, marking the foundation day of the Election Commission of India, is observed every year on:
e: National Voters' Day is observed on 25 January, the foundation day of the Election Commission of India in 1950, to encourage voter enrolment and participation.

q: World No Tobacco Day, observed under the aegis of the World Health Organization, is observed every year on:
e: World No Tobacco Day is observed on 31 May every year under the World Health Organization to highlight the health risks of tobacco use.

q: International Olympic Day, marking the founding of the International Olympic Committee in 1894, is observed every year on:
e: International Olympic Day is observed on 23 June, marking the founding of the International Olympic Committee at Paris in 1894.

q: The invention of the compound microscope (around 1590) is generally credited to the Dutch spectacle-maker:
e: The compound microscope of around 1590, using two lenses in a tube, is generally credited to the Dutch spectacle-maker Zacharias Janssen.

q: The miners' safety lamp, which greatly reduced explosions in coal mines, was invented in 1815 by:
e: Humphry Davy invented the miners' safety lamp in 1815; its flame was enclosed by wire gauze, which prevented it from igniting firedamp in coal mines.

q: The Mohs scale, devised by the German geologist Friedrich Mohs, is used to measure the:
e: The Mohs scale, devised by Friedrich Mohs, ranks minerals by hardness from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond), based on which mineral can scratch another.

q: The Beaufort scale is used to measure the:
e: The Beaufort scale measures wind force, grading it from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane) by its observed effects on sea and land.

q: A 'light year', the measure in which the distances of stars are commonly expressed, is a unit of:
e: A light year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres, so it is a unit of distance, not of time.

q: Reykjavik is the capital of:
e: Reykjavik is the capital of Iceland, the island country in the North Atlantic, and is the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state.

q: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of:
e: Ulaanbaatar is the capital and largest city of Mongolia, the landlocked country between Russia and China.

q: Bucharest is the capital of:
e: Bucharest is the capital and largest city of Romania, situated on the Dambovita river in the south of the country.

q: The currency of Norway is the:
e: Norway's currency is the krone (Norwegian crown); Norway is not an EU member and has not adopted the euro.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC), the dedicated market-borrowing arm of Indian Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation, Indian Railways' dedicated market-borrowing arm, was incorporated in 1986 to raise funds for railway assets.

q: The Container Corporation of India Limited (CONCOR), the container train operator of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: The Container Corporation of India (CONCOR) was incorporated in 1988 and took over container operations and inland container depots from Indian Railways.

q: RITES Limited, the transport infrastructure consultancy company of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: RITES Limited, the transport infrastructure consultancy of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in 1974 as Rail India Technical and Economic Services.

q: The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC), the catering and online ticketing arm of Indian Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: IRCTC, which handles catering, tourism and online railway ticketing, was incorporated in 1999 as a public sector undertaking of the Ministry of Railways.

q: Burn Standard Company Limited, the wagon-building public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: Burn Standard Company Limited, the wagon-building undertaking under the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in 1976 after nationalisation of Burn and Co.

q: The Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation (IRSDC), set up as a joint venture of RLDA and IRCON for redevelopment of railway stations, was incorporated in the year:
e: The Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation, a joint venture of RLDA and IRCON for station redevelopment, was incorporated in 2012.

q: The headquarters of the Indian Railways Welfare Organisation (IRWO), which builds housing colonies for railway employees, is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Indian Railway Welfare Organisation, which builds housing colonies for railway employees, is located in New Delhi.

q: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Limited (DMRC), which built and operates the Delhi Metro network, is a joint venture of:

options.A: The Government of India and the Government of Haryana
options.B: The Government of NCT of Delhi and the Municipal Corporation of Delhi
options.C: The Government of India and the Government of Uttar Pradesh
options.D: The Government of India and the Government of NCT of Delhi

e: DMRC is a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of NCT of Delhi, each holding equal equity in the corporation.

q: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Limited (DMRC) was registered as a company in the year:
e: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation was registered as a company in 1995, after which construction of the Delhi Metro began in 1998.

q: The Centre for Advanced Maintenance Technology (CAMTECH) of Indian Railways, located at Gwalior, functions as a directorate under the:
e: CAMTECH at Gwalior, which works on maintenance technology for Indian Railways, functions as a directorate under the RDSO at Lucknow.

q: The Konkan Railway line between Roha and Thokur (near Mangaluru), built by the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited, was dedicated to the nation in the year:
e: The Konkan Railway line between Roha and Thokur, built by Konkan Railway Corporation, was dedicated to the nation in 1998 after completion of the full route.

q: The locomotive township of Chittaranjan in West Bengal, where the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works is located, is named after the freedom fighter:
e: Chittaranjan township in West Bengal is named after Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das, the freedom fighter, and houses the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works.

q: The Patiala Locomotive Works (PLW) at Patiala, which manufactures and remanufactures diesel and electric locomotives, was originally set up in 1981 as the:
e: The Patiala unit was set up in 1981 as the Diesel Component Works for overhauling diesel locomotive components; it later became Diesel Modernisation Works and PLW.

q: Rail Bhawan, the headquarters building of the Ministry of Railways at New Delhi, is located on the road named:
e: Rail Bhawan, the headquarters of the Ministry of Railways in New Delhi, stands on Raisina Road, near Parliament House.

q: The Electric Loco Shed at Visakhapatnam, which homes electric locomotives operating on the East Coast, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Electric Loco Shed at Visakhapatnam homes locomotives of the Waltair side of the East Coast, and it functions under the East Coast Railway zone.

q: The Diesel Loco Shed at Villupuram in Tamil Nadu functions under which zonal railway?
e: Villupuram in Tamil Nadu lies in the Tiruchchirappalli division area of the Southern Railway, under which its diesel loco shed functions.

q: The Kurduvadi Workshop in Maharashtra, known for the overhaul of narrow gauge rolling stock, functions under which zonal railway?
e: Kurduvadi Workshop in Maharashtra, known for narrow gauge rolling stock work, lies on and functions under the Central Railway.

q: The MEMU Car Shed at Bhilai in Chhattisgarh, which maintains mainline electric multiple unit rakes, functions under which zonal railway?
e: Bhilai in Chhattisgarh is in the Raipur division of the South East Central Railway, under which the MEMU Car Shed at Bhilai functions.

q: The EMU Car Shed at Virar, which maintains suburban electric multiple unit rakes of the Mumbai suburban network, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: Virar is on Mumbai's western suburban line, which is operated by Western Railway, so the EMU Car Shed at Virar belongs to Western Railway.

q: The Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Memorial Hospital at Byculla in Mumbai is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Memorial Hospital at Byculla, Mumbai, is the headquarters hospital of Central Railway.

q: The railway station with the shortest name in India, 'Ib', is located in the State of:
e: Ib, a station named after the Ib river, is the shortest station name in India and is located in Odisha, near Jharsuguda.

q: The EMU Car Shed at Tikiapara, which maintains the suburban electric multiple unit rakes operating from Howrah, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The EMU Car Shed at Tikiapara is a South Eastern Railway installation under the Kharagpur division; it maintains the suburban EMU rakes that run from Howrah over South Eastern Railway sections.

q: Naharlagun, the broad-gauge railhead serving the Itanagar capital region, is located in the State of:
e: Naharlagun, the broad gauge railhead serving the Itanagar capital region, is located in Arunachal Pradesh.

q: The Railway Hospital at Perambur in Chennai is the headquarters hospital of which zonal railway?
e: The Railway Hospital at Perambur in Chennai, attached to the ICF area, is the headquarters hospital of Southern Railway.

q: In the divisional organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'Sr. DEE', borne by the head of the electrical branch, stands for:
e: Sr. DEE expands to Senior Divisional Electrical Engineer, the head of the electrical branch of a railway division.

q: In the divisional organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'Sr. DME', borne by the head of the mechanical branch, stands for:
e: Sr. DME expands to Senior Divisional Mechanical Engineer, the head of the mechanical branch of a railway division.

q: In the divisional organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'Sr. DSTE', borne by the head of the signalling and telecommunication branch, stands for:

options.A: Senior Divisional Stores and Transport Engineer
options.B: Senior Divisional Safety and Traffic Engineer
options.C: Senior Divisional Systems and Telecommunication Engineer
options.D: Senior Divisional Signal and Telecommunication Engineer

e: Sr. DSTE expands to Senior Divisional Signal and Telecommunication Engineer, the head of the S and T branch of a division.

q: In the divisional organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'Sr. DMM', borne by the head of the materials management branch, stands for:
e: Sr. DMM expands to Senior Divisional Materials Manager, the head of the materials management (stores) branch of a division.

q: In the divisional organisation of Indian Railways, the designation 'Sr. DSC', borne by the head of the security branch (RPF), stands for:
e: Sr. DSC expands to Senior Divisional Security Commissioner, the head of the Railway Protection Force security branch of a division.

q: In the Railway Board, the designation 'PED', borne by the heads of directorates in the Board's office, stands for:
e: In the Railway Board, PED stands for Principal Executive Director, the level at which heads of Board directorates function.

q: In the Railway Board, the designation 'AM', borne by the officers heading directorates below the level of the Members of the Board, stands for:
e: In the Railway Board, AM stands for Additional Member, the officers heading directorates below the Members of the Board.

q: In railway signalling, the trackside equipment 'MSDAC', used for detecting the presence of trains in track sections, stands for:
e: MSDAC stands for Multi Section Digital Axle Counter, trackside equipment that counts axles in and out to detect train presence in track sections.

q: In the traction distribution organisation of Indian Railways, the overhead equipment installation 'SSP' stands for:
e: In traction distribution, SSP stands for Sub-Sectioning and Paralleling Post, an OHE installation between sectioning posts in 25 kV AC traction.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'RCT', denoting the tribunal which adjudicates claims for compensation and refund of fares, stands for:
e: RCT stands for Railway Claims Tribunal, the tribunal that adjudicates compensation claims and fare refund claims against the railways.

q: In railway recruitment, the abbreviation 'RRC', denoting the zonal body which conducts recruitment to erstwhile Group 'D' posts, stands for:
e: RRC stands for Railway Recruitment Cell, the zonal body that conducts recruitment to erstwhile Group D posts on each zonal railway.

q: India's first Vistadome coach service, introduced in April 2017 for tourists on a scenic ghat section, was run between Visakhapatnam and:
e: India's first Vistadome coach service of April 2017 ran between Visakhapatnam and Araku, letting tourists view the scenic Eastern Ghats section.

q: The first section of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, dedicated to the nation in January 2021, was the section between:
e: The first Western Dedicated Freight Corridor section dedicated in January 2021 was the 306 km Rewari to Madar section in Haryana and Rajasthan.

q: Which State became the first in India to have a fully (100 per cent) electrified broad gauge railway network, achieving the milestone in 2023?
e: Haryana became the first state in India to achieve 100 per cent electrification of its broad gauge railway network, reaching the milestone in 2023.

q: The first air-conditioned suburban local train service of Mumbai, introduced in December 2017 on the Western Railway, was run between Borivali and:
e: Mumbai's first air-conditioned suburban local, introduced in December 2017 on Western Railway, ran between Borivali and Churchgate.

q: The first section of the Pune Metro, opened for public service in March 2022, was run between Vanaz and:
e: The first section of the Pune Metro opened in March 2022 ran between Vanaz and Garware College on the Vanaz to Ramwadi corridor.

q: The first section of the Ahmedabad Metro, inaugurated in March 2019, was run between Vastral Gam and:
e: The first section of the Ahmedabad Metro, inaugurated in March 2019, ran between Vastral Gam and Apparel Park on the east-west corridor.

q: The first section of the Nagpur Metro, opened for public service in March 2019, was run between Sitabuldi Interchange and:
e: The first section of the Nagpur Metro opened in March 2019 ran between Sitabuldi Interchange and Khapri on the north-south corridor.

q: The world's first hydrogen-powered passenger train, the Coradia iLint, entered commercial service in 2018 in the country of:
e: The Coradia iLint, the world's first hydrogen-powered passenger train, entered commercial service in Germany in 2018.

q: The first Yuva Express of Indian Railways, introduced in 2010 with fully air-conditioned accommodation aimed at young passengers, was run between Howrah and:
e: The first Yuva Express, a fully air-conditioned train for young passengers introduced in 2010, ran between Howrah and New Delhi.

q: The first Jan Shatabdi Express, introduced in 2002 as an affordable variant of the Shatabdi Express, was run between Mumbai and:
e: The first Jan Shatabdi Express, introduced in 2002 as a cheaper Shatabdi variant, ran between Mumbai and Madgaon on the Konkan route.

q: The tragedy 'Othello', centred on the Moorish general Othello and his ensign Iago, was written by:
e: Othello is a tragedy by William Shakespeare, in which the Moorish general Othello is manipulated by his ensign Iago into destroying his wife Desdemona.

q: The novel 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame' (1831), centred on the bell-ringer Quasimodo and the dancer Esmeralda in Paris, was written by:
e: The Hunchback of Notre-Dame (1831), set in Paris around the bell-ringer Quasimodo and Esmeralda, was written by the French author Victor Hugo.

q: The novel 'Adventures of Huckleberry Finn' (1884), centred on Huck Finn and the escaped slave Jim on the Mississippi River, was written by:
e: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1884) was written by Mark Twain, the pen name of Samuel Clemens, and follows Huck and Jim down the Mississippi.

q: The collection of short stories 'Dubliners' (1914), portraying middle-class life in the Irish capital, was written by:
e: Dubliners (1914), a collection of fifteen stories of Dublin life, was written by the Irish author James Joyce.

q: The novel 'Lolita' (1955), narrated by the literature professor Humbert Humbert, was written by:
e: Lolita (1955), narrated by Humbert Humbert, was written by the Russian-American novelist Vladimir Nabokov.

q: The historical mystery novel 'The Name of the Rose' (1980), set in an Italian abbey in 1327, was written by:
e: The Name of the Rose (1980), a mystery set in a medieval Italian abbey, was written by the Italian author and scholar Umberto Eco.

q: The popular science book 'Cosmos' (1980), based on the celebrated television series of the same name, was written by:
e: Cosmos (1980), the companion book to the famous television series on the universe, was written by astronomer Carl Sagan.

q: The book 'Guns, Germs, and Steel' (1997), which examines how geography and environment shaped the fates of human societies, was written by:
e: Guns, Germs, and Steel (1997), which explains how geography and environment shaped societies, was written by Jared Diamond.

q: The work 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936), originally prepared as a speech that could not be delivered, was written by:
e: Annihilation of Caste (1936) was written by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar as an undelivered speech arguing that caste must be destroyed to reform Hindu society.

q: The Sanskrit play 'Malavikagnimitram', centred on King Agnimitra and the dancer Malavika, was written by:
e: Malavikagnimitram, the Sanskrit play about King Agnimitra and the dancer Malavika, was written by Kalidasa.

q: The Sanskrit devotional poem 'Gita Govinda', celebrating the love of Lord Krishna and Radha, was composed by:
e: The Gita Govinda, the Sanskrit devotional poem on the love of Krishna and Radha, was composed by the poet Jayadeva.

q: The 'Akbarnama', the official chronicle of the reign of Emperor Akbar, was written by:
e: The Akbarnama, the official Persian chronicle of Akbar's reign, was written by Abul Fazl, one of the nine gems of Akbar's court.

q: The Hindi epic poem 'Saket' (1931), which retells the Ramayana story centred on Urmila, the wife of Lakshmana, was written by:
e: Saket (1931), the Hindi epic centred on Urmila, wife of Lakshmana, was written by Maithili Sharan Gupt, the Rashtrakavi.

q: The celebrated Hindi poem 'Kurukshetra' (1946), reflecting on war and peace through the Mahabharata, was written by:
e: Kurukshetra (1946), the Hindi poem reflecting on war and peace through the Mahabharata, was written by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar.

q: The novel 'The Vendor of Sweets' (1967), centred on the sweet-maker Jagan and his son Mali in Malgudi, was written by:
e: The Vendor of Sweets (1967), set in Malgudi around the sweet-maker Jagan and his son Mali, was written by R. K. Narayan.

q: The novel 'Nectar in a Sieve' (1954), depicting the life of the peasant woman Rukmani in a changing Indian village, was written by:
e: Nectar in a Sieve (1954), the story of the peasant woman Rukmani, was written by Kamala Markandaya.

q: The book 'Homo Deus: A Brief History of Tomorrow' (2015), the sequel to 'Sapiens', was written by:
e: Homo Deus: A Brief History of Tomorrow (2015), the sequel to Sapiens, was written by Yuval Noah Harari.

q: The novel 'A Farewell to Arms' (1929), centred on an American ambulance driver on the Italian front in the First World War, was written by:
e: A Farewell to Arms (1929), set on the Italian front in the First World War, was written by Ernest Hemingway, who had himself served as an ambulance driver.

q: The Famine Inquiry Commission (1944), appointed to investigate the Bengal famine of 1943, was chaired by:
e: The Famine Inquiry Commission of 1944, which investigated the Bengal famine of 1943, was chaired by Sir John Woodhead.

q: The JVP Committee (1948), named after the initials of its three members, was set up to re-examine the question of:

options.A: The integration of the princely States
options.B: The reorganisation of provinces on a linguistic basis
options.D: The location of the new capital of India

e: The JVP Committee of 1948, named from Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya, re-examined reorganisation of provinces on a linguistic basis.

q: The Mahajan Commission (1966), chaired by former Chief Justice Mehr Chand Mahajan, was appointed to resolve:
e: The Mahajan Commission of 1966, chaired by Mehr Chand Mahajan, was appointed to resolve the Maharashtra-Karnataka border dispute over Belagavi and other areas.

q: The first Law Commission of independent India, set up in 1955, was chaired by:
e: The first Law Commission of independent India, set up in 1955, was chaired by M. C. Setalvad, the first Attorney General of India.

q: The Expert Committee to Revise and Strengthen the Monetary Policy Framework, which submitted its report to the Reserve Bank of India in 2014, was chaired by:
e: The 2014 Expert Committee to revise the monetary policy framework, which proposed inflation targeting, was chaired by RBI Deputy Governor Urjit Patel.

q: The FRBM Review Committee, constituted by the Government of India in 2016 to review the working of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, was chaired by:
e: The FRBM Review Committee of 2016, which recommended a debt anchor and a fiscal council, was chaired by N. K. Singh.

q: The Committee for Consultations on the Situation in Andhra Pradesh (2010), appointed to examine the demand for a separate State of Telangana, was chaired by:
e: The committee that examined the Telangana statehood demand in 2010, after consultations in Andhra Pradesh, was chaired by Justice B. N. Srikrishna.
